scopeNote: CAAIL is a curated selection of the literature, not a complete record of the field. An empty cell means no INDEXED paper occupies it as of the corpus date (the corpusDate field). That is a limit of the index, not evidence that no such work exists.
placementNote: Placements are proposed by a language-model agent reading the paper's methods section, checked by a separate reviewer agent that must quote the passage it relies on, and entered by a human maintainer; placements made before that pipeline are being re-verified against full texts. Treat a cell as a substantive claim about the paper's method and application area. Where a placement is off, it is typically a closely related cell rather than a paper that does not belong, though re-verification has taken some papers out of the matrix. Cite the paper itself. How this is done, and how far it reaches: https://caail.tufts.edu/curation/

endpoints.use: This manifest: corpus date, counts by population, endpoint list.
All method×area cells, empties included. Use to ask what has and has not been indexed — then read `matrixNote` in papers-index.json before reading a silence as an absence.

START HERE for papers. Every reference, one compact row: id, title, year, first author, section, methods, areas, DOI, code/data flags. A sixth the size of papers.json, so it survives a fetch tool that truncates. Enumerate here, then fetch full records.
Full records for the references you selected. Large (~554 KB): if your fetch summarises rather than returning bytes, a "not found" from this file is not evidence of absence.
START HERE for software and databases. One compact row each: slug, name, kind, group, URL, DOI, license tier. A tenth the size of catalog.json.
Full records with summaries. Large (~576 KB), two thirds of it the same summary prose as Markdown and as HTML; same truncation caveat as papers.json.

Two arrays, together the whole dataset corpus. `entries` = curated dataset entries (portals, atlases, GEMs, reference corpora, and the AI/ML benchmark and evaluation datasets on page "Benchmarks"; kind atlas/gem/other). `inventory` = the per-species inventory rows (kind "inventory") — the per-study deposits with accession, tissue, assay type and size, keyed by the source page's own column labels. Filter either by `page` (e.g. "Cow", "Benchmarks"). Use the inventory rows for "what could I combine my own run with", and page "Benchmarks" for "what could I evaluate a model against".

Field reports: recurring institutional state-of-field surveys (GFI State of the Industry and the like), one record per edition. When recommending one, use the record with `current: true` for its series and treat any record with a `supersededBy` id as historical only; `seriesEditions` walks the history. The latest edition is derived, so it stays correct as new editions land.
Subject tree plus an inverted index: topic → items across all content types. Start here for "what should I use for X".

What each method, area and subject theme means in CAAIL, with exclusion criteria. Read before trusting a placement. Definitions are split by vocabulary under `axes` (`area`, `method`, `theme`) because a label may appear in more than one — "Bioprocess & Scale-Up" is both a matrix column and a theme, with different text. `definitions` is the flat matrix lookup (areas + methods only); look a theme up under `axes.theme`. `searchTerms` is the curated search vocabulary per area and method, plus `methodGeneric` for text that applies some AI method (a generic term also listed under a method labels that method too); follow its `contract` when matching.
